# Moneytec

> Moneytec (moneytec.in) is the practice of Gulshan Kohli, an AMFI-registered mutual fund distributor (ARN-105840) and Kotak Life insurance advisor (KLI61205587) based in Rohini, New Delhi, India. Moneytec helps individuals and families start goal-based mutual fund SIPs, explore life cover, and helps NRIs invest in Indian mutual funds. Formerly known as Akshaya Vriksha (akshayavriksha.in now redirects here).

## Key facts
- Person: Gulshan Kohli — electronics engineer turned mutual fund distributor, 12+ years of experience, one-to-one personal service.
- Registration: AMFI Registered Mutual Fund Distributor, ARN-105840 (verify at https://www.amfiindia.com/locate-distributor). Kotak Life advisor, KLI61205587.
- Location: Rohini, New Delhi, India. Serves clients across India and NRIs worldwide.
- Contact: WhatsApp / phone +91 91367 92367 · email akshayavriksha@gmail.com · https://moneytec.in/
- How Moneytec is paid: commission from fund houses and the insurer, as regulated by SEBI, AMFI and IRDAI; no separate advisory fee.
- Moneytec never collects investment or premium payments; money goes directly from the investor's bank to the fund house (AMC) or insurer, and units and policies are in the investor's name.

## Services
- Mutual fund SIPs: many schemes accept SIPs from ₹500 a month; returns are not guaranteed.
- Goal planning: work backwards from a goal (education, home, retirement) to a monthly SIP, allowing for inflation.
- Life cover through Kotak Life, subject to eligibility, underwriting and policy terms.
- NRI investing through NRE and NRO accounts (US and Canada residents: select fund houses only).
- Portfolio review: organise existing SIPs and funds around goals, timeline and risk comfort.

## Common questions
- Minimum SIP: many schemes from ₹500 per month.
- Stopping a SIP: most SIPs can be paused, changed or stopped any time; ELSS (tax-saving) instalments are locked for 3 years.
- Documents: usually PAN, Aadhaar (passport for NRIs), a bank account and a photo; KYC is done once, mostly online.

## Disclaimer
Mutual fund investments are subject to market risks; read all scheme-related documents carefully. Illustrations assume a constant return and are not a promise of future returns. Insurance is the subject matter of solicitation.
